title: Card everything
summary: Wrapping every section in a rounded container weakens hierarchy when the containers do not represent meaningful grouping or interaction.
problem: AI-generated interfaces frequently use cards as the default layout primitive, creating unnecessary boundaries, nested surfaces, and visual noise.
use_when: Auditing dashboards, settings pages, and generated marketing/product screens
A layout contains repeated bordered or elevated surfaces with no semantic grouping
avoid_when: The card represents a genuinely independent object or action target
The information must remain grouped when reordered, scanned, or displayed responsively
rationale: Whitespace, typography, alignment, and dividers can establish hierarchy without adding another surface.
Excess containers consume visual attention and reduce the difference between important and ordinary groups.
Cards are useful when their boundary carries meaning; the anti-pattern is indiscriminate use, not cards themselves.

signals: most page sections use identical card chrome
removing a border/background would not reduce comprehension
